newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN BUILDING WORKERS THREATEN GAUTENG STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN BUILDING WORKERS THREATEN GAUTENG STRIKE.

text.p: South Africa's Construction and Allied Workers Union said on Saturday its members would go ahead with a building workers' strike in Gauteng on Monday after conciliation failed to break a deadlock in wage negotiations.
Arbitration will, however, also start on Monday to determine whether the strike will be unlawful, as maintained by employers, the union said in statement.
"Until the arbitrator makes the award, members of CAWU will definitely commence with strike action on Monday, February 17," the union said.

Conciliation was held on February 10 and 14. The wage talks first deadlocked in August last year. CAWU is demanding a raise of one rand an hour for semi-skilled and general workers. Other issues in dispute are paternity and maternity leave provisions.
